header.name: Anthropology of Violence - 1
header.description:
This is a hard class. Regular reading and active engagement in class is key.

Violence, at first glance, appears obvious, self-evident. Yet upon closer inspection, what counts as violence, we find, is contingent, shifting, and is as much the function of the one who seeks to determine its emergence. This course begins with the 'emergence' of violence as an anthropological category. What are the social and cultural conditions of possibility of the emergence of violence? This is the first axis of investigation. Next, we examine the production of violence, that is, perpetration, both latent and emergent. The goal in this section is to examine the socialisation of the perpetrator. We do this through case studies from around the world, and look at different 'violent figures' - the headhunter, the mercenary, the serial killer to name a few. Finally we look at the temporal unfolding of violence - its duration in social life. We examine different analytical frames of temporality - the descent of violence into the ordinary rhythms of everyday life, the anticipation of violence, and the aftermath.
